issue: No-envelope XM key-off must cut channel volume while retaining recoverable sample phase
scope: Fourteen authored scores:nine PCM/activity failures and five healthy controls. Both default-rate stereo and post-row activity directions were verified. A natural-end control remains silent under volume restore. Fixtures have no volume envelope or fadeout; decoder guards assert those ignored counts are zero.
observed: Note97/K00/delayed K03 followed by a note without instrument wrongly resume audio after release.
Explicit channel volume,instrument-default and fine-volume restores are wrongly blocked; same-row volume/default cases are included.
Primary FT2 keyOff sets realVol/outVol to zero when no volume envelope is enabled. With zero fadeout,volume commands can restore the active sample; no new note is required.
Current native held=false also stops the sample after its gain ramp reaches zero. Any fix must preserve phase,not merely make later commands audible.
qualification: Forced intended media comparison decoded the authored companion and failed at the first PCM byte after the restore boundary. The actual worker fails at generation0 packet2 PCM with matching PTS/byte count. This does not independently prove a pre-fix seek failure.

The first worker attempt had an unrelated expected-duration error: XmAudioReader appends a120ms release tail. The fixture metadata was corrected from480/360ms to600/480ms. That initial log is retained and is not worker PCM proof.

At baseline there was no production change or accepted ID. Do not change the supported envelope/fadeout profile or claim full FT2 bit-exact mixing. Independent C00/split-row controls model channel-volume semantics in the existing renderer profile.
prototype_scope: Standalone adapter compares the actual decoder and candidate helper at two rates and mono/stereo. All56 actual/reference PCM pairs match after the candidate;all56 reference streams remain byte-for-byte unchanged. This is supplementary and does not replace Cargo or actual worker acceptance.
implementation: The actual active sample owner determines volume-envelope presence. No-envelope release sets channel volume0 while retaining phase; unsupported-envelope release keeps its former profile. Immediate note97/K00 and delayed Kxx use one helper. Existing selected/playing instrument ownership and natural sample end remain intact.

related_migration.reason: The pre-existing released-control incorrectly required a no-envelope note97 followed by explicit volume64 to remain silent. Primary FT2 keyOff semantics and the new independent controls require restoring the continuing sample phase. The same actual score,phase assertions,seek/EOF checks and natural-end silence control remain. Only its independent reference changes to C00 then volume64,and audible_after becomes true.
